propositions: The judge's Pass-2/Pass-3 decision on individual findings lacks sufficient self-consistency across repeated runs (measured via Fleiss' kappa and raw agreement over 50 G6/E4/T3 findings x 3 votes each).

The gate verdict (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) changes when plan sections are reordered, indicating order sensitivity in the judge despite use of absolute rubric scoring (measured via kappa and raw agreement over 14 plans x 3 distinct permutations each).
Infra-level INDETERMINATE outcomes (llm_unavailable or verify_failed) must be distinguished from genuine judge-INDETERMINATE and excluded/re-run to measure only stable judge decisions.
Agreement must meet dual floor: Fleiss' kappa >= 0.6 AND raw agreement >= 0.8, with sub-floor results blocking R5 (self-consistency) and R3 (order-shuffle) respectively.
The existing gate's judge reliability is a prerequisite before R5 can safely add the new asserted_capability_confirmed sub-answer and before R3 can rely on container-criteria routing.
